title: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)

sections.label: Tuition costs and DSA tutors
sections.summary: A family pays over $500 monthly for Secondary 1 tuition, over 10% of household income, while DSA portfolio tutors charge up to $300 per hour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: When I asked for more details, they shared that they are paying more than $500 for their eldest, a Secondary 1 student, for tuition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The tuition fee is more than 10% of their household income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And as though the $1-billion academic tuition industry needs another boost, another form of tuition for Direct School Admissions (DSA) has arisen.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It was reported that there are tutors who can help pupils build DSA portfolios at the rate of up to $300 per hour.

sections.label: Levelling playing field update
sections.summary: The speaker seeks an update from the Minister on further levelling the playing field for students of lower socio-economic backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Page: 7 It leaves me to seek an update from the Minister on how he intends to: One, further level the playing field for students of lower socio-economic backgrounds.

sections.label: SkillsFuture toolkit from Primary 5
sections.summary: Minister Heng announced a SkillsFuture or future-ready toolkit available from Primary 5.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Minister Heng has announced a SkillsFuture or a future-ready toolkit that will be available from Primary 5.

sections.label: Education support and inclusion initiatives
sections.summary: The passage proposes academic and non-academic support schemes, graduate service during holidays or gap years, co-locating special schools, and addressing societal painpoints.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One, develop academic and non-academic support schemes so that those who are stronger in some areas can buddy and coach those who are less so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Two, encourage graduates to make use of their school holidays or gap years to serve students at risk, localising the "Teach for America" model that is quite well-known to suit our specific local needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Third, go for bolder and more audacious initiatives, such as co-locating and co-running special schools within mainstream school compounds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Four, help address key painpoints in society that are often talked about and not easily resolved, such as the homeless, the karang guni peddlers, families with members with rare diseases or other severe disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As the captain of the education industry, it has to not only address its near-term challenges but also envision and transform itself to be a key game changer so that Singapore will be future-proof and will be here for many more 50 years to come.

sections.label: Expanding CCA intakes by tiers
sections.summary: The speaker proposes schools expand CCA intakes to different ability tiers, such as Tier 1 and Tier 2 netball teams, instead of restricting participation through trials.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But having trials to see how good they are before they are allowed to be part of a particular sport or ensemble unnecessarily restricts participation and does not allow late bloomers the space to blossom.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would propose that our schools expand their CCA intakes to take in different tiers of student abilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, a school can have a Tier 1 netball team to compete in national schools' competitions and a Tier 2 netball team to train students in the sport or even have friendly matches with other schools' Tier 2 teams.

sections.label: DSA flexibility, streams, special needs
sections.summary: The speaker urges greater DSA flexibility for less popular schools, abolishing academic streams, and including more students with special needs in mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Similarly, I would also like to urge the Ministry to help the less popular schools attract a more diverse student population, such as those who have talents in both the non-academic and academic arenas, by allowing these schools greater flexibility and autonomy to admit more students through DSA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One, as the PSLE grading system will be tweaked, I call on the Ministry, once again, to consider abolishing the academic streams.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Sorting our students according to academic streams has served its purpose during our efficiency-driven education era.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But now, as we try to move away from putting too much emphasis on scores and instead allow students to learn different subjects at different levels of difficulty, according to their abilities, let us go one step further and remove these self-limiting but no longer necessary labelling which we call Gifted, Special, Express, Normal (Academic) or Normal (Technical) streams.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Let us recognise that students develop differently and at different rates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We have already allowed subject-based banding and allowed students in the current Normal (Academic) stream to take some Express stream subjects because they are able, for instance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Let us now be bold enough to remove the labels entirely and yet continue allowing our students to learn different subjects at different levels of difficulty according to their abilities and progress.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Second, in our bid to make our schools more inclusive, I would urge the Ministry to include more students with special needs in our mainstream schools, as long as they are able to cope with the rigour and expectations of the curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although we have AED(LBS) in all our primary schools, it is not quite so for our secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To mitigate the challenge of not being able to employ enough AED(LBS), I hope the Ministry would consider my earlier suggestion to train suitable parent volunteers to take on this role.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Ministry has taken steps to reduce competition in PSLE scores.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We stopped announcing the top PSLE scorers since 2012 and stopped revealing the highest and lowest scores in a cohort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Despite these changes, the PSLE remains a high-stakes examination for 12-year-olds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Without T-scores, children and parents will still be in a race to achieve the "best" grade bands to secure a place in the "good" schools.

sections.label: MOE school programmes
sections.summary: MOE is developing diverse school programmes to meet different children's needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: MOE is developing diverse programmes in schools to meet the needs of different children.

sections.label: PSLE grading and cohort size
sections.summary: It asks how to make PSLE grading less stressful and broader, noting the 2015 Secondary 1 cohort was 38,600, about 10% lower than the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: How can we improve our PSLE system of grading and make it less stressful, broader and free up more time and space for them to pursue other interests outside of academics?

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Indeed, the 2015 cohort of 38,600 Secondary 1 students is about 10% lower than the previous year.

sections.label: Per capita primary school funding
sections.summary: Rosyth Primary School receives $7.8 million more per year than Bendemeer Primary School, a disparity it says must be addressed as smaller schools face budget constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Based on per capita funding per primary school, Rosyth Primary School is effectively receiving $7.8 million more than Bendemeer Primary School every year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: This disparity is significant and needs to be addressed because smaller schools will always face a budget constraint by default.

sections.label: Funding data and Secondary 1 posting
sections.summary: It urges the Ministry to release funding data and proposes direct admission to a chosen secondary school for top-tier PSLE students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: These schools will also be able to do more in sports and enrichment programmes which, I strongly believe, are important activities for small neighbourhood schools to build character and instil a sense of belonging and pride in their students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to release such funding data so that all stakeholders can have a meaningful discussion over this mantra that every school is a good school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Next, I wish to suggest a fundamental change to the Secondary 1 posting in the context of every school is a good school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I propose that graduating students finishing in the top tier of their primary school based on PSLE results, to be given direct admission to a secondary school of their choice.

sections.label: Equitable school funding commitment
sections.summary: The disparity decreased to about 10% in FY2015, which it calls a step in the right direction, but the Ministry must commit to 100% equitable funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In FY2015, the disparity decreased to about 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But the Ministry needs to commit to 100% equitable funding for all schools.

sections.label: Neighbourhood schools' disposable funds
sections.summary: Neighbourhood schools currently have less disposable funds than independent schools, putting them at a distinct disadvantage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, neighbourhood schools have less disposable funds than independent schools, putting them at a distinct disadvantage.

sections.label: EduSave and exam fee waiver
sections.summary: The Ministry extended EduSave contributions to all Singaporean students and extended the national examination fee waiver to all Singaporean students in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Ministry took a big step forward by extending EduSave contributions to all Singaporean students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Upon deliberation and discussion, the national examination fee waiver was also extended to all Singaporean students in 2015.

sections.label: MOE KPIs in Budget Book
sections.summary: The MOE KPIs in the 2016 Budget Book are still heavily skewed towards academic credentials, stressing the number of passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The MOE KPIs in the 2016 Budget Book are still heavily skewed towards academic credentials, stressing the number of passes and so on.

sections.label: Child-led PTM and suggested KPIs
sections.summary: A child led the PTM explaining their work, and the speaker suggests MOE design KPIs for softer qualities, such as students' self-initiated projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It was the child who led the PTM by explaining to their own parents in front of the teacher what they have done that term, what they will try to do next term and so on, with the teacher's facilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I suggest that MOE give some thought to designing and measuring KPIs for such softer but critical qualities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One such KPI that I would like to suggest is the number of students' self-initiated projects which enjoy positive peer and teacher reviews and can sustain a critical mass of student participation, encouraging our students to initiate their own projects in an entrepreneurial way and breed these kinds of qualities.

sections.label: CCAs integration and exclusivity
sections.summary: CCAs foster integration and deepen students' sense of belonging and responsibility, but may have become more exclusive in cost and push for deliverable results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: CCAs also foster integration and deepen the students' sense of belonging and responsibility towards the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, CCAs may have increasingly become more exclusive in two respects: the cost of taking part in them and the push for deliverable results.

sections.label: Niche CCAs and closed CCAs
sections.summary: Niche CCAs may have more teachers and students to share, and there are stories of schools closing popular CCAs unable to deliver quantifiable results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is even more so if the CCA is known to be a niche CCA that the school is supposedly good at, where, presumably, you have more teachers and fellow students with much to share.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are also stories of schools that have closed down popular CCAs because they have been unable to deliver quantifiable results.

sections.label: Teach for Singapore proposal
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Ministry to consider a "Teach for Singapore" programme matching exceptionally motivated teachers to underprivileged students needing closer attention and motivation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There will be students coming from underprivileged backgrounds who will need closer attention and motivation, and there are teachers who are, by nature, more caring and motivated to go the extra mile to change the lives of their students.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I ask that the Ministry consider establishing a "Teach for Singapore" programme to match exceptionally motivated teachers to underprivileged students.

sections.label: Teach for Singapore programme
sections.summary: Practising teachers could apply to join a one-year diploma programme and be deployed as fellows for three years to schools with many students on financial assistance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Practising teachers could apply to join "Teach for Singapore", with a select group chosen each year to train in a one-year diploma programme in counselling, cultural sensitivity and teaching for social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Graduates could then be deployed as "Teach for Singapore" fellows for three years to schools with a high number of students on financial assistance. "Teach for Singapore" alumni are then free to develop their teaching career.

sections.label: Class sizes OECD and MOE
sections.summary: Average OECD class sizes are 21 at primary and 24 at lower secondary, while MOE plans for 30 and 40 students per class.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Page: 17 Mdm Chair, the average class sizes at primary and lower secondary levels in the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries are 21 and 24 respectively, while MOE's planning parameters are for 30 students per class at lower primary and 40 at upper primary and secondary levels.

sections.label: Reducing class sizes request
sections.summary: Citing falling student enrolment, the speaker asks the Minister to consider reducing class sizes to the OECD and GEP equivalent instead of closing and merging schools.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In line with falling student enrolment numbers and instead of closing down schools and merging them, I ask the Minister to again consider reducing class sizes to the OECD and GEP equivalent.

sections.label: Emotional and critical learning
sections.summary: The proposal focuses on emotional and critical learning in children and young people, addressing responses to loss and life changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Specifically, I am proposing for a focus on emotional and critical learning in children and young people, where responses to issues of loss and changes Page: 18 in life are addressed.

sections.label: Reading sessions in curriculum
sections.summary: Quoting Keith Oatley on fiction building empathy, the speaker suggests reading sessions become part of the primary and secondary core curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Allow me to quote from an article by Keith Oatley, Professor Emeritus of cognitive psychology at the University of Toronto: "The process of entering imagined worlds of fiction builds empathy and improves your ability to take another person's point of view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It can even change your personality...The emotional empathy that is critical to our day-to-day relationships also enables us to picture ourselves living as the characters do when we read fiction." I would like to suggest that reading sessions become part of our primary and secondary schools' core curriculum and not merely an exercise within the English class.

sections.label: Loss in syllabus
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the topic of loss be included in the syllabus at all levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to suggest the topic of loss be included in the syllabus at all levels.

sections.label: Teacher workload and training
sections.summary: The speaker says teachers are swamped and hopes more teachers can be employed and trained for these teaching areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As it is, the teachers are already swamped with work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope that more teachers can be employed, specifically trained to manage these areas of teaching, where a lighter touch is needed and where a safe environment is crucial.

sections.label: Suggestions to MOE and ministries
sections.summary: The speaker says the message is that we care about you, and hopes MOE with MCCY and MSF will consider the suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The message is simple: we care about you and not just how well you do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These are some of my suggestions which I hope MOE, in partnership with the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), will consider.

sections.label: Children using portable infocomm equipment
sections.summary: A 2014 survey found 54% of children aged seven to 14 and 92% of those aged 15 to 24 use portable infocomm equipment for wireless Internet.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: According to the "Annual Survey on Infocomm Usage in Households and by Individuals 2014", 54% of our children aged between seven and 14, and 92% of our young aged 15 to 24 use portable infocomm equipment to connect to the Internet wirelessly.

sections.label: Cyber Wellness programmes update request
sections.summary: The speaker asks for an update on Cyber Wellness programmes in schools and IHLs and what other cyber safety initiatives will be implemented.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Page: 20 Hence, may I ask the Ministry for an update on the Cyber Wellness programmes in our schools and whether they also include IHLs?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry also share what other initiatives will be implemented to promote cyber safety?

sections.label: Schools and healthy eating habits
sections.summary: The speaker says schools have an important role in fostering healthy eating habits and commends MOE and HPB for the Healthy Meals in Schools programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao
sentences.text: Our schools, therefore, have an important role to play to help foster healthy eating habits and food preferences in young Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao
sentences.text: I wish to commend MOE and the Health Promotion Board (HPB) for their efforts in the area, resulting in the "Healthy Meals in Schools" programme in 2016.

sections.label: School partnerships with parents and community
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOE plans to support schools in strengthening partnerships with parents and the community, noting the registration system does not prioritise proximity alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As Stephen Covey said "Synergy catalyses, unifies and unleashes the greatest power within people".

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to know whether MOE has plans to give more support to the schools to strengthen partnerships of schools with parents and the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Our current primary school registration system does not give priority purely based on proximity to schools.

sections.label: Primary school priority system review
sections.summary: A speaker urges MOE to review the primary school priority system, discouraging parents living more than five kilometres away and prioritising nearby students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I urge MOE to review the current primary school priority system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: We should discourage parents living more than five kilometres away from the school from sending their child to the school and give greater priority to students living near the school.

sections.label: Preschool non-attendance figures
sections.summary: MSF figures show children aged five to six not attending preschool fell from about 5% in 2006 to 0.8% in 2012, remaining below 1% in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Based on an earlier reply from MSF, the number of children of ages five to six who do not attend any form of preschool has declined from about 5% in 2006 to 0.8% in 2012 and, in 2015, this figure remains below 1%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: This is encouraging as efforts to reach out to their families have shown success.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: However, there is still the 1% or so, or around 250 children each year.

sections.label: Compulsory education before Primary 1
sections.summary: A speaker proposes MOE bring compulsory education forward, ideally starting at Kindergarten 1 but at least at Kindergarten 2.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: I would propose that MOE look into bringing forward compulsory education to before Primary 1.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: It would be ideal to start compulsory education at the Kindergarten 1 (K1) level, but it would be good enough, for now, to begin compulsory education at the K2 level.

sections.label: MOE and partner kindergartens
sections.summary: There are currently 15 MOE-run kindergartens, including new ones this year, and 169 run by partner operators.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Currently, there are 15 MOE-run kindergartens, including the new ones to be set up this year, as well as 169 run by partner operators.

sections.label: Preschoolers with developmental issues
sections.summary: The number of preschoolers diagnosed with developmental issues such as speech and language delays, learning difficulties and autism spectrum disorders has trended upward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Over the years, there has been an upward trend in the number of preschoolers diagnosed with developmental issues like speech and language delays, learning difficulties and autism spectrum disorders.

sections.label: After-school care ballot demand
sections.summary: A 2014 news report revealed demand for after-school care vacancies was so overwhelming that some primary schools hold ballots to enrol students.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: A news report in 2014 revealed that the demand for vacancies in after-school care services was so overwhelming that in some primary schools, they are holding ballots to enrol their students in their student care services.

sections.label: Student care centre expansion
sections.summary: The Ministry announced plans to increase student care centres to about 120 by 2015.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: The Ministry had announced plans to increase the number of student care centres to about 120 by 2015.

sections.label: Preschool education and MOE Kindergartens
sections.summary: MOE began piloting MOE Kindergartens in 2014 to offer quality, affordable preschool education, with 15 centres now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Bill Gates said, "The first five years have so much to do with how the next 80 turns out." The importance of preschool education cannot be underestimated and, hence, we must make it a priority to invest in preschool education so that we open the doors of opportunity to every child and help them acquire the skills they need for a meaningful learning to realise their dreams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Hence, I was heartened that MOE started piloting MOE Kindergartens (MKs) in 2014 to offer quality and affordable pre-school education, and there are now 15 such centres.

sections.label: Disability support in tertiary institutions
sections.summary: Disability Support Offices were set up in 2014 in publicly-funded tertiary institutions, and students with impairments may tap the SEN fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: The setting up of Disability Support Offices (DSOs) in 2014 in all publicly-funded tertiary institutions was a great step of facilitation for students with disabilities in such institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: In addition, Singaporean students with physical or sensory-related impairments who are in such tertiary institutions may tap upon the Special Education Needs (SEN) fund to purchase assistive technology devices and supporting services, such as signing interpretation and Braille printing.

sections.label: Support for students with special needs
sections.summary: As of July 2015, 81 secondary schools each had one AED(LBS), and newly-recruited allied educators must attend an NIE diploma programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: As of July 2015, 81 secondary schools have each been resourced with one AED(LBS) to support students with mild SENs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: About 10% to 20% of teachers in every mainstream school are trained to have a deeper knowledge and skills to support students with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: In addition, all newly-recruited allied educators are required to attend a one-year, full-time Diploma in Special Education Programme conducted by the National Institute of Education (NIE).

sections.label: Shift away from academics
sections.summary: The speaker will discuss making a paradigm shift away from an over-emphasis on academics to prepare children and people for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Today, I will be speaking about what we must do differently and how to make a paradigm shift away from an over-emphasis on academics, in order to better prepare our children and people for the future.

sections.label: Narrow emphasis on academics
sections.summary: Despite efforts towards holistic education, there is still a narrow emphasis on academics and paper qualifications.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Currently, despite our efforts to move towards a holistic education, there is still a narrow emphasis on academics and paper qualifications.

sections.label: Balance in students' education
sections.summary: The passage states a need for better balance in students' education journey by dialling back excessive focus on academics.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We need a better balance in our students' education journey.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: This means dialling back the excessive focus on academics.

sections.label: MOE paradigm shift three ways
sections.summary: MOE will emphasise non-academic learning, reduce focus on academic results, and recognise more forms of merit and achievement.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: On MOE's part, we will address this paradigm shift in three ways: one, we will put more emphasis on non-academic aspects of learning; two, we will reduce excessive focus on academic results; and three, we will offer more opportunities for different forms of merit and achievements to be recognised.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar, Mr Seah Kian Peng, Mr Leon Perera and Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin touched on the importance of non-academic learning as part of holistic education.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: I agree fully that good character, socio-emotional competencies and other skills like critical thinking and effective communication are necessary foundations for work and life.

sections.label: Holistic Development Profile report card
sections.summary: A Holistic Development Profile of each child is provided in the report card given to parents at each school year's end.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: At the end of each school year, a Holistic Development Profile of each child is provided in the report card given to parents.

sections.label: Enhanced cohort camp experiences
sections.summary: Cohort camp experiences for all students will be enhanced as part of the National Outdoor Adventure Education Master Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Going forward, I am happy to announce that we will enhance the cohort camp experiences for all students as part of our National Outdoor Adventure Education Master Plan.

sections.label: Five-day Secondary 3 OBS camp
sections.summary: A five-day expedition-based camp at Outward Bound School will be piloted from 2017 and rolled out from 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The school cohort camps and OE in PE lessons will lead up to a five-day expedition-based camp for all Secondary 3 students held at the Outward Bound School (OBS) on Coney Island and Pulau Ubin.

sentences.text: In addition, we will introduce another 20 new ELPs, covering 10 additional sectors in accountancy, air transport, electronics, energy and chemicals, facilities management, healthcare, hotel, maritime, spatial design, and visual communication.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This will bring the total number of ELPs to 37, covering 22 sectors.

sections.label: Credit age limit and transferability
sections.summary: There is no upper age limit for the Credit, but the Credit is not transferrable.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We want every Singaporean, young and old, to think about this personal enterprise that cannot be transferred or outsourced to someone else.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, in response to Mr Ang Wei Neng, while there is no upper age limit for the Credit, the Credit is also not transferrable.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit usage figures
sections.summary: From January to March, about 18,000 individuals used SkillsFuture Credit, with about $5.2 million disbursed, and 17% were aged 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: From January to March this year, about 18,000 individuals have utilised their SkillsFuture Credit, with about $5.2 million disbursed.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: What is encouraging is that 17% of them are aged 60 and above.

sections.label: Courses, disability support, coaching concerns
sections.summary: About 2,500 courses were added by this month, and MOE and MSF will jointly review the Post-Secondary Education Account and SkillsFuture Credit to better support persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: By this month, we will have added about 2,500 courses to the list of eligible courses from just about four months ago.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Ms Denise Phua and Ms Chia Yong Yong have spoken about helping persons with disabilities learn skills and offered some specific suggestions.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I have spoken to Minister Tan Chuan-Jin on this and we decided that between MOE and MSF, we will do a joint review on the Post-Secondary Education Account plus the SkillsFuture Credit, look at it together, rationalise and adjust it so that we can better support persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As for life or executive coaching suggested by Mr Ang Hin Kee, we need to recognise that many of these are one-to-one sessions and are susceptible to abuse: you know, you coach me, I coach you, both of us collect $500 from the Government.

sections.label: Global reputation of universities
sections.summary: They score best for strong global reputation among academics and employers, which accounts for 50% of the weightage.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Not because of the number of foreign students or foreign faculty, but they score best for their strong global reputation among academics and employers, which accounts for 50% of the weightage.

sections.label: Local faculty share comparison caveat
sections.summary: Harvard, MIT and Oxford have a similar share of local faculty as our universities, but data bases and definitions differ, so comparisons may not be apples to apples.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Harvard, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and Oxford have a similar share of local faculty as our universities, but I have a big caveat here because when we look at it, the bases of compiling the data and definitions are very different, and so we may not be comparing apples to apples.

sections.label: Developing deep research expertise
sections.summary: In research, we must develop deep, differentiated expertise highly relevant to Singapore and of active interest to the world.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In research, we must, over time, develop deep, differentiated expertise highly relevant to Singapore and which the world takes an active interest in, whether it is water sufficiency, biodiversity, diabetes, urban planning or education.

sections.label: Approval reason for proposal
sections.summary: He approved this particular proposal among many because it was good science and relevant to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I asked him why Page: 58 he approved this particular one among so many proposals.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: He said because it was good science and it was relevant to Singapore.

sections.label: NTU and NUS satellite leaders
sections.summary: Assoc Prof Low Kay Soon and Prof Goh Cher Hiang lead NTU's Satellite Research Centre and NUS' Satellite Programme, and led six Singapore satellites' design, construction and launch last year.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Low Kay Soon and Prof Goh Cher Hiang respectively lead NTU's Satellite Research Centre and NUS' Satellite Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They led the design, construction and launch of six Singapore satellites last year.

sections.label: Research talent and social science
sections.summary: The Singapore Teaching and Academic Research Talent Scheme and the Social Science Research Council platform will provide local academics opportunities to propose research on Singapore's social development.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In this effort, we will leverage the Singapore Teaching and Academic Research Talent Scheme that was launched last year.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will also use the platform of the Social Science Research Council to provide opportunities for local academics to put up their proposals to conduct research into areas that are important to Singapore's social development.

sections.label: Holistic education and aptitude admissions
sections.summary: The vision of higher performance requires dialling back excessive focus on academics and paper qualifications, focusing on outdoor education, PSLE review, more choices, lifelong mastery and aptitude-based admission into IHLs.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Our vision of higher performance centres on the intrinsic worth and potential of a student, a vision that requires a dial-back from any excessive focus on academics and paper qualifications at all levels.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We also want to focus on other aspects of learning; therefore, outdoor education, a review of the PSLE system, offer more choices and opportunities across all levels, focus on lifelong building of mastery and move towards aptitude-based admission into our IHLs.

sections.label: Arts and music programmes growth
sections.summary: Students' exposure to the arts is enhanced, with four more secondary schools offering Enhanced Art or Music programmes and three more centres hosting Art or Music Elective programmes, while diploma and degree enrolment increased.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We want to harness this further by enhancing students' exposure to the arts and providing more opportunities for students with talent and passion to deepen their learning and pursue it at the tertiary level and beyond.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This year, four more secondary schools began offering the Enhanced Art or Music programmes, benefiting more than 300 students in the 10 schools offering these programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In addition, three more centres began hosting Art or Music Elective programmes, with students from over 30 schools selected through demonstrations of their talents and not their PSLE scores.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Enrolment into diploma-level courses increased by around 30% from 2006 to 2015, and by about 40% in degree-level courses from 2010 to 2015.

sections.label: PEIs offering degree programmes
sections.summary: In response to Mr Ang Wei Neng, 50 PEIs offered degree programmes in 2015, with a student intake of around 21,500 Singaporeans and foreigners.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In response to Mr Ang Wei Neng, 50 PEIs offered degree programmes in 2015, with a student intake of around 21,500 Singaporeans and foreigners.

sections.label: MOE holistic development changes
sections.summary: MOE will continue developing children holistically by reducing emphasis on academic results and offering multiple pathways, making changes to the PSLE and increasing aptitude-based admissions at IHLs.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: MOE will continue to focus on developing our children holistically by reducing the emphasis on academic results and offering multiple pathways to success.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Hence, we are making several changes to the PSLE and increasing aptitude-based admissions at IHLs.

sections.label: Parent Support Groups in schools
sections.summary: Parents can get support from other parents through PSGs in their children's schools, such as Mr Juraiman Rahim who joined Northland Primary PSG in 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Parents can get support from other parents through PSGs in their children's schools.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For example, Mr Juraiman Rahim joined the Northland Primary PSG in 2014.

sections.label: ECG counsellors industry sharing sessions
sections.summary: In February, 68 MOE ECG counsellors and WDA career coaches attended industry sharing sessions by experienced personnel from ECDA and SPRING Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Just a few months back in February, 68 MOE ECG counsellors and WDA career coaches attended industry sharing sessions by experienced personnel from ECDA and SPRING Singapore.

sections.label: ECG counsellors and career coaches
sections.summary: Counsellors visited Keppel Offshore and Marine, WDA and e2i career coaches will guide training decisions, and ECG counsellors are being recruited for schools, polytechnics and ITE colleges.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: For instance, the counsellors visited Keppel Offshore and Marine last month.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Page: 62 We will also leverage the existing pool of over 100 career coaches at WDA and e2i to provide individuals with an understanding of industry needs to better guide training decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: As WDA restructures, part of the agency – as hon Members would know from the earlier press release – will come under MOE, and the career coaches will be under MOM's wing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: ECG counsellors, such as Dorothea, Noormala and Muhd Faizal, are helping our young people discover their talents and interests, who, in turn, are more sure of what their next steps could be.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We are on track to having close to 100 ECG counsellors serving all schools, polytechnics and ITE colleges by end-2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We agree, which is why we are taking great care to select suitable candidates with attributes, such as passion to work with young people, a positive and encouraging nature, and excellent interpersonal, communication and networking skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We have filled nearly all positions for trained ECG counsellors at our polytechnics and ITEs – 47 out of 48.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We have also recruited 14 ECG counsellors to support our secondary schools and junior colleges.

sections.label: Sector coordinators appointed
sections.summary: They have appointed sector coordinators for 10 more sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Today, we are pleased to reveal that we have appointed sector coordinators for 10 more sectors.

sections.label: Contract with WDA
sections.summary: It still has a contract with WDA to work in partnership until 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, if I remember correctly, it still has a contract with WDA to work in partnership until 2019.

sections.label: Student care centres rollout plan
sections.summary: The Member asks the Minister of State how MOE plans to roll out student care centres in all schools by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Chairman, I would like to ask the Minister of State regarding student care centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: I am quite glad to hear that all schools will have student care centres by 2020. my first clarification is: how does MOE plan to roll out this plan?

sections.label: Student care centre rollout factors
sections.summary: The rollout of student care centres depends on various factors, with quality provision availability being key to reaching every school.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The rollout will depend on a variety of factors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But the key issue for when a centre can develop and how long it will take us to reach a centre in every school is the availability of quality provision for student care centres.

sections.label: Appeal for this year's admission
sections.summary: The Ministry will look into an appeal for this year's admission for an individual who has attempted three times.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: So, my clarification, Madam, is whether, for an individual like that who has attempted three times, the Ministry would consider his case for this year's admission rather than wait till next year where he has to wait yet another year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I confirm that I have received her appeal and we will look into it.

sections.label: Normal (Technical) class size and pilot
sections.summary: Normal (Technical) class size goes down to 20 in Spectra and Crest secondary schools, and an OE learning and physical disabilities pilot will be implemented in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Where the class size of Normal (Technical) is concerned, in Spectra and Crest secondary schools, we go down to 20 per class to meet those needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: On OE learning and physical disabilities, we are running a pilot programme and it will be implemented in 2017.

sections.label: Art or Music Elective Programme centres
sections.summary: Three more centres host Art or Music Elective Programme, enabling students like Leonard Chia from Kent Ridge Secondary School to take the courses.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: With regard to the second question, what we have now is we have three more centres which are already hosting Art or Music Elective Programme (AEP), whereby students who are interested can also be routed to these centres.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: It is this student from Kent Ridge Secondary School, Leonard Chia.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: He did not get a place in a school which offered AEP but because of the three centres that we have, they enabled students like him to be able to have opportunities to take on the courses.

sections.label: Dropout rates reduced
sections.summary: A combination of different things done has reduced dropout rates to less than 1%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: With the combination of different things that we have done, we have reduced dropout rates to less than 1%.

sections.label: Transfers and subject-based banding
sections.summary: Normal (Academic) students who do well may transfer to Express, and under subject-based banding students good at Mathematics may take it at Express level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Even where we have, let us say, a Normal (Academic) student who has done well, we will permit transfer to the Express course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: For specific subjects, under subject-based banding, if we see a student who is very good at Mathematics and may be in Normal (Academic), we do permit and encourage him to take Mathematics at the Express level.

sections.label: SkillsFuture plan for MOE
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture plan for MOE will comprise the following components.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture plan for MOE will comprise the following.

sections.label: Employability coaches in system
sections.summary: NTUC's e2i and WDA have over 200 employability coaches who have coached for 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As the Member knows, in NTUC, they set up e2i, which is a tripartite organisation with about 100 employability coaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Likewise, when we set up WDA in 2003, we also took in all the employability coaches from the Community Development Councils (CDCs) and on the ground, that is, another 100-plus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, we have over 200 people in the system who have done this for the last 10 years: meeting industry, meeting jobseekers and giving coaching.

sections.label: Primary 1 and 2 support
sections.summary: Students in Primary 1 and 2 who cannot catch up are moved to smaller classes with dedicated teachers for up to two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In Primary 1 and 2, as I had mentioned, if students joining our schools are not able to catch up, we take them out of the form class into a smaller size of maybe eight to 10 students and we provide dedicated teaching resource, one or two teachers, to level them up in English or literacy or numeracy skills, for up to two years.

sections.label: School mergers and falling enrolment
sections.summary: Falling cohort size makes school mergers necessary, as low enrolment schools cannot afford programmes and CCAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: With reference to school mergers, falling cohort size is a reality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Enrolment is coming down across the different schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: It would not be right to roll back enrolment in a healthy secondary school to bolster up the lowered enrolment in the other secondary schools because this would lead to a distortion of outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: If you do not have the critical mass in low enrolment schools, we will not be able to afford the programmes, the CCAs that Members have also mentioned.
